definition: An open reasoning model appearing across 11 sources in three distinct roles. As a subject it is the archive's high-water mark for monitorability, scoring 78.3 percent average and exceeding its own non-reasoning sibling by 32.8 points on the cue where the gap is widest -- one of the corpus's clearest pieces of evidence that reasoning training makes a model's stated reasoning more informative about its behaviour, not less. As a source of traces it is upstream of much of the archive: several methods warm-start on millions of its responses, and the distilled checkpoints derived from it are among the most-used backbones here. As an instrument it filters candidates, reviews queries and judges outputs in benchmark construction -- one source notes its benchmark is model-mediated at nearly every step, with this model filtering confusable candidates and reviewing queries while human involvement is confined to adjudicating disagreements. Its measured limits: on symbolic variabilisation of competition problems it is among the most robust models on the easier set (-3.6 percent) and still degrades on the harder ones (81.5 to 61.3 on one), and across open reasoning models including this one, fewer than 25 percent of reasoning traces comply with instructions given for the reasoning itself.

evidence.note: Scores each reasoning step of a translation by how much appending it raises a frozen reference model's teacher-forced likelihood of the gold translation, and adds that as a dense per-step reward on top of sequence-level quality — after first establishing that explicit reasoning helps long and hard inputs while drifting on terminology and style.
evidence.title: PAMT: Process-Aligned Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Domain Machine Translation

evidence.note: Formalizes test-time scaling as budgeted inference over a model's implicit prefix tree, separates three structurally different regimes that a single scalar budget conflates, specifies what a reproducible inference protocol must declare, and releases 1.9 million traces — with the empirical section showing a selection score that makes accuracy fall from 75.56% to 65.83% as the candidate bank grows.
evidence.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility

evidence.note: Turns table-to-report generation into Monte Carlo tree search over partial reports, scored by a reward that verifies every numerical claim by generating and executing SQL against the source table rather than by asking a judge — and keeps that search reward strictly separate from the benchmark's own evaluator to avoid a reward-hacking loop.
evidence.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search for Table-to-Multimodal Report Generation

evidence.note: Bolts a small trainable recurrent block between a frozen 1.1B language model's body and its output head, so reasoning happens as repeated refinement of two latent vectors rather than as generated tokens.
evidence.title: Think Deep, Speak Once: Relit, A Recursive Latent Implicit Transformer Framework

evidence.note: Uses chain-of-thought about required capabilities as training-time supervision for a skill retriever -- distilled from a teacher in stage one and refined by retrieval-rewarded GRPO in stage two -- so that at inference the model encodes the bare query with no generation at all.
evidence.title: SkillReason: Reasoning-Enhanced Agent Skill Retrieval for Implicit User Requests

evidence.note: Explores in weight space rather than token space during RLVR by sampling policies from a variational posterior at rollout time, and introduces a training-time exploration metric -- how often a method produces a correct rollout on a prompt where GRPO produced none -- because entropy and pass@k cannot tell exploration from degeneration.
evidence.title: Parameter Exploration for RLVR via Variational Learning

evidence.note: Benchmarks whether reasoning models follow instructions inside their reasoning traces, finding under 25% compliance at best and worse as difficulty rises.
evidence.title: ReasonIF: Large Reasoning Models Fail to Follow Instructions During Reasoning

evidence.note: Defines certaindex, an algorithm-agnostic measure of how much a reasoning algorithm's answer has stopped changing, and builds it into a serving system that reallocates or terminates compute per query — saving up to 50% of tokens in batch inference and tripling online throughput.
evidence.title: Efficiently Scaling LLM Reasoning with Certaindex

evidence.note: Argues that faithfulness alone is insufficient for CoT monitoring and adds verbosity — whether the trace lists every factor needed to solve the task — combining the two into a monitorability score, then shows models can look faithful while omitting key factors.
evidence.title: Measuring Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Faithfulness and Verbosity

evidence.note: A position paper arguing that reading a reasoning model's intermediate tokens as 'reasoning' or 'thinking' is unsupported by the available evidence and actively harmful, and collating experiments in which trace semantics and solution accuracy come apart.
evidence.title: Position: Stop Anthropomorphizing Intermediate Tokens as Reasoning/Thinking Traces!

evidence.note: Reads a reasoning trajectory as a multi-step pseudo-gradient descent on the model's own parameters, which makes each token an optimization step, the trajectory an inner loop, and the training regime a meta-learning problem in which the question is the task.
evidence.title: Deciphering Trajectory-Aided LLM Reasoning: An Optimization Perspective

name: DeepSeek-R1
